request.request_text:
PUBLIC RECORDS ACT REQUEST – STRUCTURAL DEFICIT / LABOR COST CONTAINMENT RECORDS

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Gov. Code § 7920 et seq., I request copies of the following records created, received, transmitted, or maintained between January 1, 2025 and the date this request is processed.

Statement of Purpose

This request concerns the City's public representations about structural deficit solutions and whether labor cost containment options have been evaluated in addition to tax increases and service reductions. The requester is a Berkeley resident with a direct interest in the City's budget decision-making process.

Custodians

  • Mayor Adena Ishii
  • Mayor's Office staff
  • City Manager
  • Deputy City Managers
  • Finance Director
  • Human Resources Director
  • City Clerk
  • IT Department (including email archives and document management systems)

Requested Records

1. Labor Cost Containment Analysis

Records reflecting proposed, planned, evaluated, analyzed, or implemented actions concerning reduction, containment, restructuring, or slowing of City labor costs associated with the City of Berkeley's structural General Fund deficit, including but not limited to actions concerning: salaries; pension costs; CalPERS costs; employee pension contribution pickup (EPMC); employer-paid member contributions; retiree healthcare/OPEB liabilities; overtime; staffing levels; headcount reduction; hiring freezes; layoffs; furloughs; compensation growth; labor agreements; productivity or efficiency reforms; departmental reorganization; or changes to employee benefits.

This request includes records reflecting final recommendations, adopted strategies, and analyses that were presented to or relied upon by elected officials, department heads, or the City Council, including but not limited to materials underlying public budget presentations and the analytical work, scenario modeling, options analyses, and comparative studies that preceded, informed, or were considered in preparing those presentations, whether or not such materials were included in Council agenda packets.

2. Employee Pension Contribution and Cost-Sharing Analysis

Records reflecting analysis or evaluation of requiring employees to assume a greater share of pension contribution costs, including records concerning: employee pension contribution pickup (EPMC); employer-paid member contributions; cost-sharing arrangements; comparisons to other California cities; or estimated fiscal impact of such changes.

This request includes records reflecting final recommendations, adopted strategies, and analyses that were presented to or relied upon by elected officials, department heads, or the City Council, including but not limited to materials underlying public budget presentations and the analytical work, scenario modeling, options analyses, and comparative studies that preceded, informed, or were considered in preparing those presentations, whether or not such materials were included in Council agenda packets.

3. Budget-Balancing Strategy Comparisons

Records reflecting budget-balancing strategies evaluated, analyzed, compared, proposed, planned, or implemented for the FY2027–2028 biennial budget that involve or compare: tax increases; service reductions; labor-cost reductions; compensation-related reforms; pension-cost containment measures; staffing reductions; or operational restructuring.

This request includes records reflecting final recommendations, adopted strategies, and analyses that were presented to or relied upon by elected officials, department heads, or the City Council, including but not limited to materials underlying public budget presentations and the analytical work, scenario modeling, options analyses, and comparative studies that preceded, informed, or were considered in preparing those presentations, whether or not such materials were included in Council agenda packets.

4(a). Communications Received from Labor Organizations

Records reflecting communications sent by any labor union, bargaining unit, labor representative, or employee association to the Mayor's Office, City Manager's Office, Finance Department, or Human Resources Department, concerning: the structural deficit; budget reductions; labor concessions; staffing reductions; pension costs; compensation; employee pension contribution pickup (EPMC); overtime; hiring freezes; or strategies to avoid layoffs.

4(b). City-Side Records Predating Formal Meet-and-Confer

Records reflecting City-side analysis, strategy, planning, or internal communications — including records created prior to the initiation of formal meet-and-confer proceedings — concerning: the structural deficit; budget reductions; labor cost containment; pension costs; compensation reform; employee pension contribution pickup (EPMC); staffing reductions; hiring freezes; or strategies to avoid layoffs.

For purposes of this request, "formal meet-and-confer proceedings" means proceedings initiated by written notice pursuant to Gov. Code § 3505, and does not include informal communications, budget briefings, informational presentations, or preliminary discussions preceding such written notice.

5. Analytical and Briefing Materials

Any memoranda, briefing materials, presentations, spreadsheets, fiscal analyses, projections, implementation plans, or staff analyses: (a) shared with bargaining units or employee associations outside of formal meet-and-confer proceedings, as defined above; (b) relied upon in preparing the FY2027–2028 proposed biennial budget; or (c) used to evaluate structural expenditure reform options related to personnel costs.

6. Records of Meetings at Which Labor Cost Options Were Discussed

Records sufficient to identify meetings, convenings, or work sessions at which structural deficit labor cost containment options were discussed, including: agendas reflecting labor cost, pension, compensation, EPMC, or staffing items; calendar invitations with subject lines or body text referencing such topics; meeting notices; and attendee lists. This request does not seek the content of oral discussions but does seek records reflecting that such discussions occurred and who participated.

Scope of "Records"

For avoidance of doubt, "records" includes emails, attachments, memoranda, presentations, spreadsheets, reports, calendar entries, meeting notes, text messages, and electronically stored information. This request encompasses communications sent or received on any device — personal or City-issued. For communications on personal devices, the City shall treat any communication concerning City business as a public record subject to disclosure, consistent with City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608.

Format

Please provide records in electronic format only. Native electronic files are preferred where reasonably available.

Partial Production

If any category of records cannot be produced in full, please produce all responsive records that can be identified and produced without resolving any disputed questions, and identify separately any records or categories being withheld or requiring additional time.

If portions of records are exempt, please redact exempt material and produce the remainder.

Regarding claimed burden: the City may satisfy this request as to any category by producing a representative sample of responsive records, provided it identifies the sample as such and describes the broader universe of withheld records.

Withholding Log

Pursuant to Gov. Code § 7923.100, if any records are withheld in whole or in part, please provide a log identifying each withheld record with sufficient particularity to allow assessment of the claimed exemption, including: (1) date; (2) type of record; (3) general subject matter without revealing exempt content; (4) author's title or department and general recipient category; (5) specific statutory exemption claimed; and (6) whether the record has been produced in redacted form or withheld in full.

Response

Please confirm receipt of this request and provide the determination required under Gov. Code § 7922.535.
